statement.text:
The First Discovered Quasar
This problem studies the radio source 3C 273. The Moon has sidereal period 27.3 days and angular diameter 30 arcminutes. Use \(3600\) arcseconds per degree, \(1\,\mathrm{pc}=3.09\times10^{16}\,\mathrm m\), \(H=75\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}\), \(c\simeq3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\), \(L_\odot=3.82\times10^{26}\,\mathrm W\), \(M_\odot=2\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}\), and \(\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{T\,m/A}\). The original occultation, spectrum and radio-image figures provide the observational data.
A.1. Lunar angular motion
Find the lunar motion against background stars in one hour, one minute, and one second. Express each in degrees, arcminutes, and arcseconds.
A.2. One lunar diameter
How long does the Moon take to move by its own angular diameter?
B.1. Occultation oscillations

What causes the intensity oscillations? Options: A, telescope diffraction pattern. B, mount instability. C, lunar surface features. D, atmosphere. Explain your choice.
B.2. Component reappearance
Why does component B not produce a separate bump at reappearance? Options: A, both orbit the Moon. B, changed line of sight. C, both align with the lunar limb at reappearance. D, one fades intrinsically. Explain what this reveals about source structure.
B.3. Angular component separation
Estimate the projected angular separation from the occultation graph and the lunar angular speed.
C.1. Spectral redshift

Compare corresponding Balmer-line wavelengths in the laboratory and 3C 273 spectra. Estimate \(z=(\lambda-\lambda_0)/\lambda_0\).
C.2. Gravitational-redshift hypothesis
If \(z=(1-2GM/(c^2r))^{-1/2}-1\), find the required mass for a source at the edge of the Galaxy, \(r\sim3\times10^{21}\,\mathrm m\), and at the edge of the Solar System, \(r\sim1.5\times10^{13}\,\mathrm m\). Explain why these are implausible.
C.3. Cosmological distance
Instead use \(z\simeq v/c\) and Hubble law \(v=Hd\). Find the distance and compare it with the Galaxy.
D.1. Spectral luminosity
The flux is \(F_\nu=25000\nu^{-0.3}\,\mathrm{Jy}\), with frequency in Hz and \(1\,\mathrm{Jy}=10^{-26}\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,Hz^{-1}}\). Find \(L_\nu=4\pi d^2F_\nu\).
D.2. Integrated radio luminosity
Integrate over \(10^7<\nu<10^{11}\,\mathrm{Hz}\).
D.3. Luminosity comparison
Compare with the stated solar luminosity and \(L_{MW}=1.5\times10^{10}L_\odot\).
E.1. Annihilation photon energy
Explain why electron-positron annihilation \(e^++e^-\to2\gamma\) at rest does not directly produce the observed optical and radio emission. Estimate photon energy and wavelength.
E.2. Accretion power
One solar mass falls from infinity to Schwarzschild radius \(R_s=2GM/c^2\) each year. Estimate Newtonian potential-energy power and compare it with D.
F.1. Minimum-energy ratio

For particle energy \(U_e\propto B^{-3/2}\) and field energy \(U_B\propto B^2\), minimize \(U=U_e+U_B\) at fixed volume and show \(U_e/U_B=4/3\).
F.2. Jet magnetic field
Take the jet energy to be half the energy radiated in one second in D.2, and volume \(10^{45}\,\mathrm{m^3}\). Estimate its magnetic field.

children.text: The angular rate is \(360^\circ/(27.3\times24\,\mathrm h)\). In one hour: \(0.54945^\circ=32.967\) arcmin \(=1978.02\) arcsec. In one minute: \(0.0091575^\circ=0.54945\) arcmin \(=32.967\) arcsec. In one second: \(0.000152625^\circ=0.0091575\) arcmin \(=0.54945\) arcsec. The source solution labels its final per-second result in degrees where arcseconds are intended.
Divide \(30\) arcminutes by \(0.54945\) arcminutes per minute to obtain \(54.6\,\mathrm{min}\).

The published key selects A. Physically, lunar occultation fringes are Fresnel diffraction at the lunar limb, recorded by the telescope. They should not be attributed to the telescope aperture alone. The other proposed instrumental and surface explanations do not account for the coherent occultation fringes. This wording discrepancy is retained for self-review.

C. The two components can have different projected separations normal to the lunar limb at disappearance and reappearance. Their reappearance times coincide because their positions align along the local limb. This constrains the two-dimensional structure.

The disappearance times differ by roughly half a minute. Multiply by \(32.97\) arcseconds per minute to obtain about \(16.5\) arcseconds, conventionally estimated as \(15\) arcseconds. Graph reading and projection limit precision.

For example, the rest H-gamma line at \(434\,\mathrm{nm}\) appears near \(500\,\mathrm{nm}\). Corresponding line ratios are approximately \(1.158\), giving \(z\simeq0.158\). Accept reasonable estimates from several lines.

Solve for \[M=\frac{c^2r}{2G}\left[1-(1+z)^{-2}\right].\] At \(z=0.158\), this gives about \(2.6\times10^{17}M_\odot\) and \(1.3\times10^9M_\odot\), respectively. Either would dominate and severely disrupt the containing Galaxy or Solar System.
\(d=zc/H=0.158\times300000/75=632\,\mathrm{Mpc}\), thousands of times the Galactic size. This is the stated low-redshift approximation, without a modern cosmological-distance correction.

Using \(d=632\,\mathrm{Mpc}=1.953\times10^{25}\,\mathrm m\), \[L_\nu=1.198\times10^{30}\nu^{-0.3}\,\mathrm{W/Hz}.\] Rounding \(d\) to \(2\times10^{25}\,\mathrm m\) gives the published coefficient \(1.25\times10^{30}\). The luminosity has units W/Hz, not the flux units printed in the answer sheet.

\[L=\frac{1.198\times10^{30}}{0.7}\left[(10^{11})^{0.7}-(10^7)^{0.7}\right]\simeq8.56\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W.\] The rounded-distance convention gives \(8.94\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W\), conventionally \(9\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W\).

The supplied benchmarks give \(L/L_\odot\simeq(2.2\text{ to }2.4)\times10^{11}\), and \(L/L_{MW}\simeq15\). These are comparisons using the given luminosity benchmarks. The solar value is a bolometric luminosity, so it should not be described as the actual solar radio-band luminosity.

Each photon has \(E=m_ec^2=0.511\,\mathrm{MeV}=8.19\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm J\), and \(\lambda=h/(m_ec)=2.43\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm m=0.00243\,\mathrm{nm}\). This is gamma radiation, far above optical and radio frequencies. The source sheet has an incorrect wavelength conversion and calls it X-rays. Reprocessing is outside this simple direct-emission comparison.

The model releases \(GM\dot M/R_s=\dot Mc^2/2\). With \(\dot M=2\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg/yr}\), \(P=2.85\times10^{39}\,\mathrm W\), enough to supply the radio luminosity even with losses. The source numerical value uses \(\dot Mc^2\), dropping its own factor one-half. This estimate is a Newtonian energy scale, not a relativistic accretion-efficiency calculation.
At the stationary point \(dU/dB=(-3U_e/2+2U_B)/B=0\), so \(U_e=4U_B/3\). It is a minimum because both energy contributions grow at opposite ends of the positive B range.

Use energy, not power: \(U\simeq4.3\text{ to }4.5\times10^{37}\,\mathrm J\). From \(U=7U_B/3\), \(U_B=3U/7\), so \[B=\sqrt{\frac{2\mu_0(3U/7)}{V}}\simeq2.2\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm T.\] The source rounds the luminosity to \(10^{38}\,\mathrm W\), yielding \(2.3\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm T\).

solution.text:
The First Discovered Quasar
A.1. Lunar angular motion
The angular rate is \(360^\circ/(27.3\times24\,\mathrm h)\). In one hour: \(0.54945^\circ=32.967\) arcmin \(=1978.02\) arcsec. In one minute: \(0.0091575^\circ=0.54945\) arcmin \(=32.967\) arcsec. In one second: \(0.000152625^\circ=0.0091575\) arcmin \(=0.54945\) arcsec. The source solution labels its final per-second result in degrees where arcseconds are intended.
A.2. One lunar diameter
Divide \(30\) arcminutes by \(0.54945\) arcminutes per minute to obtain \(54.6\,\mathrm{min}\).
B.1. Occultation oscillations
The published key selects A. Physically, lunar occultation fringes are Fresnel diffraction at the lunar limb, recorded by the telescope. They should not be attributed to the telescope aperture alone. The other proposed instrumental and surface explanations do not account for the coherent occultation fringes. This wording discrepancy is retained for self-review.
B.2. Component reappearance
C. The two components can have different projected separations normal to the lunar limb at disappearance and reappearance. Their reappearance times coincide because their positions align along the local limb. This constrains the two-dimensional structure.
B.3. Angular component separation
The disappearance times differ by roughly half a minute. Multiply by \(32.97\) arcseconds per minute to obtain about \(16.5\) arcseconds, conventionally estimated as \(15\) arcseconds. Graph reading and projection limit precision.
C.1. Spectral redshift
For example, the rest H-gamma line at \(434\,\mathrm{nm}\) appears near \(500\,\mathrm{nm}\). Corresponding line ratios are approximately \(1.158\), giving \(z\simeq0.158\). Accept reasonable estimates from several lines.
C.2. Gravitational-redshift hypothesis

C.3. Cosmological distance
\(d=zc/H=0.158\times300000/75=632\,\mathrm{Mpc}\), thousands of times the Galactic size. This is the stated low-redshift approximation, without a modern cosmological-distance correction.
D.1. Spectral luminosity
Using \(d=632\,\mathrm{Mpc}=1.953\times10^{25}\,\mathrm m\), \[L_\nu=1.198\times10^{30}\nu^{-0.3}\,\mathrm{W/Hz}.\] Rounding \(d\) to \(2\times10^{25}\,\mathrm m\) gives the published coefficient \(1.25\times10^{30}\). The luminosity has units W/Hz, not the flux units printed in the answer sheet.
D.2. Integrated radio luminosity
\[L=\frac{1.198\times10^{30}}{0.7}\left[(10^{11})^{0.7}-(10^7)^{0.7}\right]\simeq8.56\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W.\] The rounded-distance convention gives \(8.94\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W\), conventionally \(9\times10^{37}\,\mathrm W\).
D.3. Luminosity comparison
The supplied benchmarks give \(L/L_\odot\simeq(2.2\text{ to }2.4)\times10^{11}\), and \(L/L_{MW}\simeq15\). These are comparisons using the given luminosity benchmarks. The solar value is a bolometric luminosity, so it should not be described as the actual solar radio-band luminosity.

This is gamma radiation, far above optical and radio frequencies. The source sheet has an incorrect wavelength conversion and calls it X-rays. Reprocessing is outside this simple direct-emission comparison.
E.2. Accretion power
The model releases \(GM\dot M/R_s=\dot Mc^2/2\). With \(\dot M=2\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg/yr}\), \(P=2.85\times10^{39}\,\mathrm W\), enough to supply the radio luminosity even with losses. The source numerical value uses \(\dot Mc^2\), dropping its own factor one-half. This estimate is a Newtonian energy scale, not a relativistic accretion-efficiency calculation.
F.1. Minimum-energy ratio
At the stationary point \(dU/dB=(-3U_e/2+2U_B)/B=0\), so \(U_e=4U_B/3\). It is a minimum because both energy contributions grow at opposite ends of the positive B range.
F.2. Jet magnetic field
